anchor.quote: Refer to Acts of parliament using the correct style so people can find the source material. Choose when to cite the short and long titles, series numbers, jurisdiction and sections.

not_rules.note: Introductory summary advice to the writer.

anchor.quote: An Act has a short title (its name) and long title (a description). Both appear after the list of contents in the text of the Act. The long title appears as a heading before section 1 of the Act. The short title is named in section 1.
At first mention, use the short title in italics
Often, Acts also have a shorter informal title. This is usually an initialism or acronym of the short title.
Each Act has a series number to use in citations

not_rules.note: Describes what series numbers are and how they can be used.

anchor.quote: Using the series in general content helps people identify the particular Act and find it in the Legislation Register. Series are also used in annotations and in notes.

not_rules.note: Explains the purpose and utility of series numbers.

anchor.quote: Jurisdiction is an important detail

not_rules.note: Section heading grouping child guidance on indicating jurisdiction.

anchor.quote: Write a sentence that makes jurisdiction clear

not_rules.note: An alternative method / option for indicating jurisdiction.

anchor.quote: The first way is to write a sentence that explains where the Act originates. This method is useful in documents that don’t mention legislation frequently.
The basic unit of an Act is a section (s)
Choose how to cite units below section level

not_rules.note: Explicitly gives the author discretion ('You can choose which method to follow').

anchor.quote: Whether to cite at section level or below will depend on the context for your content. You can choose which method to follow.
Follow in-house style. Otherwise, be guided by the type of content you’re writing, and its purpose and audience.

not_rules.note: General advice to follow in-house style.

anchor.quote: The Constitution was enacted by the British Parliament. The long title of the Act is the Commonwealth of Australia Constitution Act 1900 (UK).
The original version is available on the UK Government Legislation website. A compilation including amendments is on the Legislation Register.
If you’re unsure, use ‘the Australian Constitution’ so there’s no confusion.

covers.quote: Style for Act titles is title case, not always italics
Use roman type for the titles of Acts in reference lists and other long lists. Blocks of italics are difficult to read.
The first time you name the Act in text, use the short title in italics.
Always use the short title in italics the first time you cite the Act in your text.

examples.note: Title case with no comma before the year

parts.quote: Export Control Act 2020
Export control Act, 2020

rules.quote: Use title case (maximal capitalisation) for the titles of Acts. Use italics for the first mention of these titles.
rules.violation_condition: the title of an Act written without title case, or not in italics on its first mention in running text
when: Use roman type for the titles of Acts in reference lists and other long lists.
Foreign legislation is written in roman type rather than italics.
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: The heading and multiple restatements prescribe title case and first-mention italics, with lists as a noted exception.

covers.quote: The year the legislation is first enacted forms part of the title.

parts.quote: Export Control Act 2020

examples.note: Contains a comma before the year

parts.quote: Export control Act, 2020

rules.quote: Don’t use a comma before the year.
rules.violation_condition: a comma placed immediately before the year in the title of an Act
rules.why: Direct negative constraint on punctuation within Act citations.

parts.quote: A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999
The Commercial Bank of Australia Limited (Merger) Act 1982 (NSW)

rules.quote: Include all the words in the title. If the title begins with ‘The’, ‘An’ or ‘A’, make sure you include it.
rules.violation_condition: an initial article ('The', 'An', or 'A') omitted from an Act's full formal title when cited
rules.why: Specific rule requiring leading articles when they form part of the official title.

parts.quote: Supply Act (No. 1) 2019–2020
Farm Household Support Amendment (Relief Measures) Act (No. 2) 2019

rules.quote: If the Act’s title has a number, include the number exactly as written. The contraction ‘No.’ retains the full stop in this situation, which is an exception to the general rule for the shortened form for ‘number’.
rules.violation_condition: the contraction 'No.' written without a period (e.g. 'No') when part of an Act's title
rules.why: Specific style rule explicitly overriding the general Australian convention for contractions.

covers.quote: After first mention, use the short title in roman type without the year

examples.note: First mention includes year in italics; subsequent mention drops the year and is in roman type.

parts.quote: … was convicted of federal offences under the Crimes Act 1914. The Crimes Act specifies …

examples.note: Subsequent reference drops the year and 'Act', in roman type.

parts.quote: … was convicted of federal offences under the Criminal Code Act 1995.The Criminal Code has a constitutional basis ...

rules.quote: If there are subsequent mentions of the Act, use the short title in roman type without the year.
rules.violation_condition: a subsequent mention of an Act that includes the enactment year or is set in italics instead of roman type
rules.why: G-4: Heading restates body; specifies formatting on subsequent mentions.

covers.quote: At first mention, include the informal title in parentheses after the title. Use the informal title after that.

examples.note: Shortened form introduced in parentheses at first mention.

parts.quote: Comcare administers the Work Health and Safety Act 2011(WHS Act). The WHS Act requires that a person who ...

examples.note: Acronym defined in parentheses at first mention.

parts.quote: … in the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 (PGPA Act). … Section 10 of the PGPA Act defines a Commonwealth entity as …

rules.quote: Add the shortened form in parentheses at the first mention if it does more than just remove the year or the word ‘Act’ from the title.
rules.violation_condition: an informal or abbreviated title introduced on subsequent mentions without having been defined in parentheses at the first mention
when: Not needed if the shortened form only drops the year or the word 'Act'.
rules.why: Defines parenthetical introduction requirements for informal shortened Act titles.

covers.quote: Or use the informal title in roman type

examples.note: FOI Act is in roman type and capitalized

parts.quote: Freedom of Information Act 1982 (FOI Act)

rules.quote: Use title case and roman type for the informal title.
rules.violation_condition: an informal title of an Act styled in italics or failing title case
rules.why: G-4: Heading restates rule in body paragraph.

covers.quote: Use the shortened form of the jurisdiction in the Act’s title in roman type and in parentheses
None of these shortened forms for jurisdictions are punctuated.

examples.note: Shortened form in parentheses in roman type without punctuation.

parts.quote: Dugong are defined as ‘fish’ for the purposes of the Marine Act 1981 (NT).

rules.quote: insert the jurisdiction’s shortened form in roman type in parentheses after the italicised title.
rules.violation_condition: a jurisdiction abbreviation following an Act title that is not enclosed in parentheses, is italicised, or uses internal full stops
when: Shortened forms must be unpunctuated: Cth, ACT, NT, NSW, Qld, SA, Tas, Vic, WA.
An alternative method is to write a sentence that explains the jurisdiction in words.
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Covers format, casing, and lack of punctuation for jurisdiction abbreviations.

covers.quote: An initial capital is correct, whether the reference is generic or not

parts.quote: Staff must read the Act to understand their compliance responsibilities.

rules.quote: Always use capitals for the words ‘Act’ and ‘Acts’ when you write about Acts of parliament.
rules.violation_condition: the word 'act' or 'acts' written in lower case when referring to Acts of parliament
rules.why: G-4: Heading restates body rule. Absolute rule requiring capitalization of 'Act(s)'.

parts.quote: ... is described in paragraph 21(3)(a).

rules.quote: Use lower case for these units unless they begin a sentence.
when: Does not apply if the word begins a sentence.
rules.why: Prescribes lower case for section, subsection, paragraph, subparagraph mid-sentence.

parts.quote: The Auditor-General’s main functions and powers are defined in Part 4 of the Act.
… under Division 2 of Part 9 of the Law Enforcement (Powers and Responsibilities) Act 2002

rules.quote: Always use an initial capital for a specific reference to a ‘Chapter’, ‘Part’, ‘Division’ or ‘Subdivision’.
rules.violation_condition: a specific reference to a Chapter, Part, Division, or Subdivision of an Act written in lower case
rules.why: Prescribes obligatory initial capitals for specific structural units.

rules.quote: Never begin a sentence with the shortened form.
rules.violation_condition: a sentence starting with an abbreviated legislative unit form (such as 'Pt', 'Div', 'Subdiv', 's', 'ss', 'subs', 'subss', 'para', 'paras', 'subpara', 'subparas')
rules.why: Clear structural constraint banning abbreviations at sentence start.

covers.quote: Don’t use a full stop after the shortened forms of units

parts.quote: ... the Copyright Act 1968, s 4.
... produce documents when required (paras 17(1)(a)–(c)).

rules.quote: Don’t use a full stop after the shortened form when you use it in a citation or note.
rules.violation_condition: a full stop placed after the shortened form of an Act unit (e.g. 's.', 'ss.', 'para.', 'Pt.') in a citation or note
rules.why: G-4: Heading restates body sentence.
